name: Open Items
rows: FY2026: July 1, 2025–June 30, 2026 · USD · Year-end audit workpapers
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · not an audit report · no opinion · the CPA reviews and concludes

Stonewick Roofing SWR-8052, June 8-24, 2026 work, is missing from the June 30 payables. The vendor asked on June 30, 2026 that it be recorded; it was paid July 15, 2026. Payables and this year's costs are understated, and book income overstated, by $2,150.00. Proposed adjustment: debit 500100 Construction contract costs, credit 210100 Accounts payable. The client decides whether to record it; the machine never posts.

Bluepine Concrete Works BPW-5120: its $250.00 change order (“Change order, added broom finish”) was never booked. It is under the $600.00 clearly trivial amount, so it is listed but not added up. If the vendor is still owed it, payables are understated by $250.00.
The FY2026 trial balance export is marked “draft and unapproved”. Every figure here rests on it. Ask Morgan Lee for the approved version and compare it with this one.

HC-COST-0100 ($3,100.00, October 8, 2025) has no readable invoice. Page 13 of the vendor invoice file, scanned at the site office, is a picture with no text layer and may be it. A person keys the invoice or requests a copy, and the pick is vouched then. The machine does not guess what a picture says.

Fernhollow Site Services FSS-0117 is billed to HANGS Holdings Inc, but the company booked and paid it (HC-COST-0733). The client says that company only holds its shares in the company, so the vendor may have addressed the wrong HANGS company. Ask the vendor which company the work was for; if it was the other company's, the company is owed the amount and its costs are overstated.

Warranty reserve: $7,400.00 of the $14,900.00 balance is left from projects completed by June 30, 2025, whose one-year warranties all ended by April 24, 2026. The $7,500.00 estimate for this year's projects has no calculation on file. Request the claims still open at June 30. The CPA judges whether the reserve is reasonable.
The $1,100.00 completion estimate for the projects completed in May was entered July 11, 2026, after year end. The client's answer 14 describes it, but no quote or calculation is on file.

HFC-26-0142 close-out legal fees are in construction cost. Every hour and rate agrees, but the invoice is for Project 4 close-out services. Moving it to estimating and bid costs would leave book income unchanged and lower the gross margin. The CPA decides.

The dividend authorization is dated June 30, 2026, but the journals were entered July 14, 2026, the operating agreement was signed July 22, 2026, and the client's answers of November 3, 2026 say the signed authorization is still being collected. Ask Morgan Lee when it was actually signed; until then neither date is relied on.

June has 60 progress payments, $186,000.00, and no receipts, about what 6.7 milestones cost. The client says June costs are completion and punch-list work on completed projects, and 3 of the 3 June picks agree, but site costs run through the same draw account and Project 5 is planned. If any June payment was for Project 5 mobilization or started Project 5 work, that cost belongs on hand at June 30. The CPA decides how much more to test.

Book income rose 249%, from $70,000.00 to $244,500.00: the price per milestone rose 10.9% and the cost per milestone 4.8%. Why prices rose faster than costs is for Morgan Lee to explain and the CPA to judge.
Materiality is proposed at $12,000.00, 5% of book income, with performance materiality $9,000.00 and clearly trivial $600.00. The engagement partner sets the final amounts.
No management representation letter has been obtained. The CPA requests it near the end of fieldwork, dated as of the report date.
These are draft workpapers and findings for the engagement partner. They are not an audit report and give no opinion. Nothing has been signed, posted or sent to the client.
